rationale: Source reading supports fixing one attributed responsibility for this Candidate without presuming a violation. restoreUserSnapshot answers every inflight logFuture with ErrAbortedByRestore and removes it from leaderState.inflight before it calls r.snapshots.Create and writes/closes the replacement sink; the public Apply contract gives ErrAbortedByRestore the definite meaning that the write effectively failed and its effects will not be present after the restore. Two effects are therefore separated by a fallible call, so the composed requirement is that the abort signal must not be delivered unless the restore really completes or the still-logged entries can no longer be committed and applied. The claim is bounded to the leader's own restore handler with a caller-supplied SnapshotStore that fails after the abort, excludes the success path, the configuration-change guard and the quorum protocol, and is offered as ready_for_check for a later direct test.

obligation.description: On the leader, answering inflight Apply/Barrier futures with ErrAbortedByRestore must not precede a user snapshot restore that then fails: the documented meaning of ErrAbortedByRestore ('the write effectively failed since its effects will not be present in the FSM after the restore') requires either a completed restore or that the entries behind those futures can no longer be committed and applied, otherwise a client receives a definite failure signal for an operation that may still be committed and consumed.

scope.description: The leader's own user-triggered restore path (Raft.Restore -> userRestoreCh -> restoreUserSnapshot) when one or more client futures are still inflight and the caller-supplied SnapshotStore fails at Create, write or close after the inflight abort loop has already run.
assumptions: The injected SnapshotStore implements the SnapshotStore interface faithfully, so Create, the sink Write or Close may return an error.
The node is Leader and the configuration guard (committedIndex == latestIndex) passes, so the handler proceeds past its early return.
The aborted futures correspond to entries already appended to the leader's LogStore.
excluded: The successful restore path, where the FSM is replaced and the burned index is appended
The outstanding-configuration-change case, which returns before the abort loop
The quorum commitment protocol itself and any consensus-safety claim
Futures answered by other error paths (ErrLeadershipLost, ErrNotLeader, ErrRaftShutdown)

parameters.failure_point: r.snapshots.Create / io.Copy(sink, reader) / sink.Close after the inflight loop

pending: A failing-SnapshotStore scenario that makes restoreUserSnapshot return an error after the inflight abort, observing the aborted future's error together with whether the entry is later counted committed and applied.

grounding.derivation: In restoreUserSnapshot the inflight loop responds ErrAbortedByRestore and removes each future from leaderState.inflight, and only afterwards does the function call r.snapshots.Create and copy/close the replacement sink; every failure there returns an error to the Restore caller (S-raft-restoresnapshot, S-api-restore). The documented contract for ErrAbortedByRestore states the write effectively failed and its effects will not be present in the FSM after the restore (S-api-restore-contract), and the callbacks that could still commit and apply the entries live on the leader's own loop independent of the inflight list (S-raft-leaderloop). The two effects are thus separated by a fallible operation, which is the responsibility this claim fixes.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the leader's user restore handler under the failing-SnapshotStore premise above; it asserts no obligation for a successful restore, for a restore refused before the abort, or for the quorum commitment protocol itself.
unresolved: Whether a SnapshotStore or sink realistically fails after the abort point in production.
Whether the aborted entries are actually counted committed and applied afterwards, which determines whether the client is truly misinformed.
alternatives: The entries may never reach commit if the leader is partitioned or replaced, in which case ErrAbortedByRestore happens to be accurate even though the abort preceded a failed restore.

bindings.description: The r.snapshots.Create call and its failure return inside restoreUserSnapshot, reached only after the inflight loop has already answered every pending logFuture with ErrAbortedByRestore.
pending: Whether the write and close steps fail for the same scenario.

associations.rationale: This is the fallible operation that separates the delivered ErrAbortedByRestore from an actually completed restore; if it fails, the futures already carry the documented 'write effectively failed' outcome while the entries remain in the log.

question.question: On the leader, restoreUserSnapshot answers every inflight logFuture with ErrAbortedByRestore before it creates and writes the replacement snapshot; if that snapshot creation, write or close then fails, do the aborted client operations really fail as the documented ErrAbortedByRestore contract states (their effects absent from the FSM), or can their log entries still be committed by the quorum and applied, so that a client is told the write effectively failed while the entry is in fact committed and consumed?
question.importance: The Apply contract gives ErrAbortedByRestore a definite meaning - the write effectively failed and its effects will not be present after the restore - which callers may rely on when deciding whether an operation needs re-issuing. If the abort is delivered before a restore that then fails, a client could treat a still-persisted entry as failed, or treat a committed entry as gone, at the A5/A7 completion boundary; a genuinely different outcome for the same reported error would be a client-contract discrepancy rather than a consensus-safety violation.
question.trigger_rationale: restoreUserSnapshot's abort loop runs before sink creation, and the documented ErrAbortedByRestore meaning is asserted in api.go; the failure handling of the snapshot store in between (sink.Cancel, error returns) is what could separate the abort from an actual restore. Because the abort and the restore are two distinct effects in one function, the ordering and the resulting committed state are not evident from the doc comment alone and merit a direct comparison under an injected failing SnapshotStore.

supporting_behavior_ids.B-quorum-commit: Context: the commitment path is independent of the inflight list, so removing aborted futures from leaderState.inflight does not by itself prevent their entries from being counted committed.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-apply-api: Consequence/contract: Apply/Barrier return the logFuture whose Error() resolves to ErrAbortedByRestore, which is the client-visible signal whose documented meaning is under test.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-config-eligibility: Prehistory/guard: restoreUserSnapshot refuses to proceed while a configuration change is outstanding (committedIndex != latestIndex), which bounds when the abort can be delivered.

contexts: Leader main goroutine handling a user-triggered restore (Raft.Restore -> userRestoreCh -> restoreUserSnapshot)
One or more client Apply/Barrier futures still in leaderState.inflight when the restore begins
Injected SnapshotStore whose Create, sink Write or sink Close fails after the inflight abort has already run
event_paths: Raft.Restore -> userRestoreCh -> leaderLoop userRestoreCh case -> restoreUserSnapshot
restoreUserSnapshot -> committedIndex != latestIndex check -> inflight loop responds ErrAbortedByRestore and removes each entry
restoreUserSnapshot -> r.snapshots.Create(version,lastIndex,term,...) fails -> return error to the Restore caller while the futures already carry ErrAbortedByRestore
leaderLoop dispatchLogs/commitment.match -> commitIndex advance -> processLogs -> FSM apply of the still-logged entries

counterevidence: restoreUserSnapshot returns before the inflight abort when a configuration change is outstanding (committedIndex != latestIndex), so the abort cannot be delivered while the cluster is mid-membership-change
On a successful restore the FSM is replaced with the snapshot contents and a burned index is appended, so ErrAbortedByRestore is accurate for the success path
The abort loop removes each future from leaderState.inflight, so this leader's inflight completion bookkeeping no longer tracks those entries
deferError.respond is single-shot, so a future answered ErrAbortedByRestore cannot later be answered nil

Whether the aborted operations' entries are still counted committed by commitment.recalculate and applied by processLogs afterwards, which would make the reported 'write effectively failed' outcome misleading for that client
Whether any consumer or caller relies on the documented ErrAbortedByRestore meaning to decide re-issuing, which would determine the practical consequence
